_comment: T4 CALIBRATION TARGETS -- ion and neutron kept SEPARATE, derived 2026-08-11
from docs/Database/FerriticSteels_RadiationDatabase_Combined.xlsx (sheets
Neutron_DislocLoops, Neutron_Voids_Swelling, Ion_DislocLoops,
Ion_Voids_Swelling).  This is NOT targets.json: that file is a live monitor
with wide bands and says so itself.  Every number here carries its source.
READ THE DOSE FIELD FIRST.  The T3 screening ran to 1.0 dpa.  NOTHING here
is measured at 1 dpa -- neutron loops are 15-32 dpa, ion loops 4-47 dpa,
ion cavities 75-650 dpa.  A calibration run must reach the dose of the
point it is being compared against, or the comparison is meaningless.
Cost is mild: the frozen-grid note measured dose 0.5->1.0 dpa as +17 % wall,
so 1 -> 30 dpa is roughly +40-60 %, NOT 30x -- it is ~1.5 more decades of a
stiff integration, not 30x the work.
MODEL <-> EXPERIMENT MAPPING.  The database reports TOTAL loop density and
ONE TEM-visible mean diameter; it does not separate <100> from 1/2<111>
except through the 'dominant Burgers vector' column.  So:
N_loop_total  <->  N_loops_100 + N_loops_111
d_loop_mean   <->  number-weighted TEM mean over both populations,
Comparing the model's d_100_nm directly against the database mean diameter
is WRONG whenever 1/2<111> is the dominant population, which it is at the
lower doses and temperatures.
f_100 must be read in the TEM-FILTERED convention at d_min = 1.0 nm
(f_100_tem_1).  Number- and content-weighted conventions differ by ~2x on
one and the same run, which is larger than any conversion parameter inside
its prior.
STATUS OF THE <100> CHANNEL.  As of the T3 campaign these observables were
WITHHELD in bin_moment mode (unvalidated closure, mean_n_100 +144 % vs a
discrete reference) AND the runs were grid-limited (topbin_100 = 1.0,
d_100 pinned at the 22.89 nm ceiling) because LOOP_NETWORK_LOSS was 0.
Do not calibrate on <100> until both are resolved.

_note: EUROFER97 only, T = 330-350 C, i.e. the T <= 400 C window the campaign
targets.  Dose rate for fast-reactor / HFR neutron is ~1e-7 dpa/s.
The 350 C point (10-15 nm, 0.8e22) is from a different heat and sits far
above the 330/335 C points; treat it as a separate point, not as scatter
F/M steels under self-ion / heavy-ion irradiation at 300-440 C.  Dose
rate is 5e-4 to 1e-3 dpa/s, i.e. ~1e4 times the neutron rate -- which is
the whole point of calibrating the two separately.
The ion CAVITY data is NOT usable at 350 C: it sits at 440-460 C and
75-650 dpa, a different regime entirely.  Calibrate ion on the LOOP
channel only, and treat cavities as a health check.
Per the instruction: share the ENERGY parameters with the neutron fit
(E_m_v, E_m_i, E_b_i2, E_b_v2, gamma_s, ...) and allow the microstructural
ones to differ (rho_d, Z_i, Z_i_loop, and the dose-rate-sensitive L_hat).

points.source: Ion_DislocLoops row 8 (Was 2025, IAEA CRP round robin)
points.caution: reported as WIDE SCATTER in both density and diameter -- it is the round-robin reproducibility study. Use as a consistency check, never as a fit point.
